title: Blade Runner 2099 – NYCC Trailer Out
excerpt: Official trailer for Blade Runner 2099 – NYCC.
body:
• Blade Runner 2099 is an 8-episode limited series premiering November 25, 2026 on Prime Video, with all episodes dropping together.
  • Michelle Yeoh plays Olwen, a Replicant nearing the end of her life; Hunter Schafer plays Cora, a human fugitive who assumes a Blade Runner's identity.
  • Set 50 years after Blade Runner 2049, the series flips the franchise's power dynamic — Replicants won the war and now hold Los Angeles.
  • The full trailer debuted at New York Comic Con on October 10, 2026, following the first teaser at San Diego Comic-Con in July.

The Blade Runner universe is expanding to television. Blade Runner 2099, an eight-episode limited series from Amazon MGM Studios and Alcon Television Group, premieres globally on Prime Video on November 25, 2026 — with all eight episodes arriving at once in more than 240 countries and territories. The full trailer debuted at New York Comic Con on October 10, 2026.

The Premise

Fifty years after the events of Blade Runner 2049, Los Angeles has been reborn — just not by humanity. A Replicant uprising and war occurred in the intervening decades. Humans lost. Replicants now hold power, and the city they rebuilt is not the rain-soaked noir metropolis of the films.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u3G6Va2lqPY

Hunter Schafer (Euphoria) plays Cora, a human fugitive who, in a final bid to stop running, takes on one last identity: a Blade Runner. She is forced to partner with Olwen, played by Michelle Yeoh (Everything Everywhere All at Once) — a Replicant with only days left to live. Together they hunt a runaway carrying a secret that could collapse their fragile city.

Showrunner Silka Luisa (Shining Girls, Halo) has described the series' visual approach as "sunshine noir" — replacing much of the franchise's signature rain and snow with hard light, heat, and deep shadows. It's a deliberate break from the aesthetic Ridley Scott established in 1982 and Denis Villeneuve extended in 2017.

The Cast

Beyond the two leads, Dimitri Abold (The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes) and Lewis Gribben (Somewhere Boy) are series regulars. The recurring guest cast is deep: Katelyn Rose Downey (The Nun II), Daniel Rigby (Renegade Nell), Johnny Harris (A Gentleman in Moscow), Amy Lennox (Only Child), Sheila Atim (The Woman King), Matthew Needham (House of the Dragon), Tom Burke (Furiosa), and Maurizio Lombardi (Ripley).

Behind the Camera

Silka Luisa serves as showrunner and executive producer alongside Ridley Scott himself, Alcon Entertainment co-founders Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, Alcon's President of Television Ben Roberts, David W. Zucker and Clayton Krueger from Scott Free Productions, Tom Spezialy, Richard Sharkey, Michael Green, Cynthia Yorkin, Frank Giustra, and Isa Dick Hackett. Jonathan van Tulleken (Shōgun) executive-produces and directed the first two episodes, setting the series' visual template.

The project was first revealed at San Diego Comic-Con in July 2026, where Yeoh, Schafer, Luisa, Kosove, and Johnson appeared before more than 6,500 fans in Hall H alongside the first teaser trailer. The October NYCC trailer is the fullest look yet at the series' tone: a city rebuilt without human hands, populated by fugitives and Replicants with nothing left to lose.

Why It Matters

The Blade Runner franchise has always worked best when it treats its worlds as inevitabilities rather than spectacles. 2099 looks committed to that fatalistic imagination — the hunted becoming the hunter, but in a world where the line between human and Replicant has blurred past recognition. Executive producer Andrew Kosove has said the series was designed to work as a standalone story, so new viewers don't need to complete the films first — though longtime fans will find direct connections to both Scott's original and Villeneuve's sequel.

For Prime Video, it's a flagship sci-fi bet heading into the holiday season — and with Yeoh coming off her Oscar win still within recent memory, the series arrives with genuine prestige-series expectations.

Premiere: November 25, 2026 — all 8 episodes, exclusively on Prime Video.
